description: CRESTE (Center for Research, Training and Education) is a collaborative, research-driven team passionate about AI, machine learning, data science, software development, and space science. We value diversity and inclusion, with female participation including a member experienced in international hackathons such as IBM and WeAreDevelopers. Through NASA Space Apps, we aim to turn scientific data into solutions that matter. Join us: developers, analysts, designers, and researchers welcome!
summary:
RotateWise is a web-based decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotations suited to their land and a changing climate. The farmer selects the farm location, and the tool loads NASA POWER Earth observation data (monthly temperature, rainfall and root-zone soil wetness) for that exact point. The farmer then adds local soil information (texture, organic matter, salinity), water access, the current cropping pattern and personal priorities: soil health, water saving, income and climate resilience.

RotateWise scores 21 crops for the site, compares thousands of possible two- or three-year rotations, and recommends the best three, each with a season-by-season plan, a score out of 100 and plain-language reasons. A stress test replans for a hotter, drier future. For example, for a Peshawar farm growing wheat and maize, the tool estimates that a rotation with lentil, mung bean, canola and sesame could cut irrigation need by about 89% and greatly improve soil health.

This matters because many farmers repeat the same crops while soils decline and water becomes scarce. RotateWise turns open NASA data into simple, local guidance.
details:
What it does and how it works
RotateWise is a single-page web tool. The farmer chooses a farm location, and the tool requests NASA POWER data for that point: monthly temperature, bias-corrected rainfall and root-zone soil wetness. It finds the local cool and warm growing seasons from the data, so it works in either hemisphere. The farmer adds soil texture, organic matter, salinity, water access, the current cropping pattern and four priorities. The tool scores 21 crops for temperature, water and soil fit, then evaluates thousands of two- or three-year rotations on soil health, water saving, income and climate resilience, weighted by the farmer’s priorities. It shows the best three rotations with a seasonal plan, scores, reasons, and a comparison with the current pattern.
Benefits and intended impact
Farmers get simple, local guidance for protecting soil and saving water. For a Peshawar wheat and maize farm, the tool estimates about 89% less irrigation need and much better soil health with a legume-based rotation. A stress test shows which rotations still work in a hotter, drier climate.
Tools used
HTML, CSS and JavaScript; the NASA POWER API; GitHub Pages for hosting. Development was assisted by AI.
Creativity
Farmers set their own priorities and see the trade-offs. They can keep a staple crop, and compare any suggestion against what they grow today.
Factors considered
Crop values are indicative agronomic estimates, not local trial data, and NASA POWER covers a wide grid cell, so results are a starting point for discussion with local agricultural experts.
